profile-list.title: Saved profile
profile-list.text:
Select a profile to edit its current revision.
Choose New profile to create another one.
Saved optimizer runs keep their own frozen revision, even after you edit or remove this profile.

profile-name.title: Profile name
profile-name.text:
A descriptive name for this plant's settings, such as a site and planning season.
You can keep several named profiles for the same plant.

profile-plant.title: Plant
profile-plant.text:
Use the exact plant identifier from your published dataset.
The workspace offers datasets that contain this plant.
It checks the demand horizon before creating a run.

horizon_days.title: Horizon (demand days)
horizon_days.text:
Number of demand days covered by the uploaded forecast.
Daily demand = forecast litres / this number.
Match the source workbook: 80 days for the Q4 source, 250 for the original annual source.
Changing this field does not convert or rescale a forecast.
A mismatch blocks the run.

demand_days_per_week.title: Demand days per week
demand_days_per_week.text:
Converts the demand horizon into productive weeks for the within-group changeover proxy.
Weeks = horizon / days per week.
Example: at 5 days per week, an 80-day forecast covers 16 weeks.
This is not a line capacity or shift schedule.

runner-classes.title: Runner classes
runner-classes.text:
Runner classes sort products by how fast they sell compared with the size of one production batch.
Each product gets one class: high, medium or low runner.

Two checks are made for every product:
1. Days: how many days of this product's sales one full batch of its base product (SEFI) would cover on its own. Few days means it sells fast.
2. Compared with the fastest: the product's days divided by the days of the fastest product of the same SEFI. 1 means it is the fastest; 5 means one batch lasts five times longer.

If the two checks give different classes, the faster class wins.
So the fastest product of each SEFI is always a high runner.

Where the classes are used:
Plant constraints can refer to them, for example "every group on line 6 needs a high runner".
SAP settings of runs made with this profile use the same classes to adjust coverage (RoC) of medium and low runners.

Saved runs keep the values they were created with. Editing them here only affects new runs.

runner_high_max_days.title: High runner: batch lasts at most (days)
runner_high_max_days.text:
A product is a high runner when one full batch would cover its sales for this many days or fewer.
Default: 10 days. Exactly 10 days counts as high.

Example: a product selling 100 L per day with a 900 L batch is covered for 9 days, so it is a high runner.

Must be lower than the low-runner days.

runner_low_min_days.title: Low runner: batch lasts at least (days)
runner_low_min_days.text:
A product is a low runner when one full batch would cover its sales for this many days or more, and the comparison with the fastest product also says low.
Default: 80 days. Exactly 80 days counts as low.

Example: a product selling 10 L per day with a 900 L batch is covered for 90 days, so by days it is a low runner.

Products between the two day values are medium runners by days.

runner_high_max_ratio.title: High runner: at most (× fastest product)
runner_high_max_ratio.text:
Compares each product with the fastest-selling product of the same SEFI.
A product is a high runner when its batch lasts at most this many times as long as the fastest product's.
Default: 3. The fastest product itself is 1, so it is always high.

Example: the fastest product is covered for 8 days and this product for 20 days. 20 / 8 = 2.5, which is at most 3, so it is a high runner even though 20 days alone would make it medium.

Must be at least 1 and lower than the low-runner value.

runner_low_min_ratio.title: Low runner: at least (× fastest product)
runner_low_min_ratio.text:
A product is a low runner when its batch lasts at least this many times as long as the fastest product's, and its days also say low.
Default: 10.

Example: the fastest product is covered for 8 days and this product for 96 days. 96 / 8 = 12, which is at least 10, so this check says low.

Values between the high and low numbers give a medium runner by this check.

cycle-stock.title: Cycle stock strategy
cycle-stock.text:
Sets how the products of one subgroup share the subgroup's coverage (RoC, days of sales one batch covers).

Single RoC: every product is filled in every batch and gets the subgroup's RoC. Best for simple sites with few products (today's behaviour).
Runner multiples: only the fastest product of a subgroup keeps the RoC. Every other product gets a whole multiple of it and is filled only every 2nd, 3rd, 4th... batch. This cuts changeovers and raises cycle stock of slow sellers (managed-complexity sites).
Optimizer chooses: the optimizer compares both versions per subgroup and keeps the better trade-off.

Coverage and changeovers of every subgroup are computed with the strategy it uses, in the optimizer, the results and SAP settings.

cycle_mode.title: Strategy
cycle_mode.text:
Single RoC: every product gets the subgroup's RoC.
Runner multiples: every subgroup uses multiples.
Optimizer chooses: each eligible subgroup is offered in both versions; the solver picks.

Example: base RoC 10 days. A product whose full batch would last 2.5 times as long as the fastest product's gets 20 days (filled every 2nd batch).

cycle_high_min_days.title: High runner: minimum RoC (days)
cycle_high_min_days.text:
Minimum multiplied RoC of a high runner that is not the fastest product of its subgroup.
Default: 0, so only the ratio to the fastest product sets its multiple.

Multiple = smallest whole number of batches that covers max(base x (1 + log10(ratio)), this minimum).

cycle_medium_min_days.title: Medium runner: minimum RoC (days)
cycle_medium_min_days.text:
Minimum multiplied RoC of a medium runner.
Default: 20 days.

Example: base RoC 10 days and a ratio of 5.8: base x (1 + log10 5.8) = 17.6 days, raised to 20, so the product is filled every 2nd batch.

cycle_low_min_days.title: Low runner: minimum RoC (days)
cycle_low_min_days.text:
Minimum multiplied RoC of a low runner.
Default: 40 days.

Example: base RoC 10 days: the product is filled at most every 4th batch.

cycle_medium_batch_factor.title: Medium runner: share of one batch
cycle_medium_batch_factor.text:
A medium runner may cover at most this share of the days one full batch would cover for it alone.
Default: 0.5.

Example: one full batch would cover 30 days and the base RoC is 10 days: at most floor(30 x 0.5 / 10) = 1, so the product stays in every batch.

cycle_max_days.title: Maximum cycle stock (days)
cycle_max_days.text:
Cap of cycle-stock days for every product.
Default: 200 days.
A multiple never makes the RoC exceed this cap. The SAP settings DC lot sizes use the same cap.

cycle_mixed_groups_only.title: Only subgroups mixing runner classes
cycle_mixed_groups_only.text:
Used with Optimizer chooses.
On (default): only subgroups whose products span two or more runner classes are offered with multiples; subgroups of similar runners keep Single RoC.
Off: every subgroup with two or more products is offered in both versions (more choice, longer solve).

runner_basis.title: Runner basis
runner_basis.text:
Sets which batch the runner class days are based on.

Fixed source reference: the source workbook's "RoC 1 full SEFI batch" (source lot size considered / the product's daily demand). This is the same value SAP settings use. No second 0.90 factor is applied.
Candidate PV: the candidate production version's effective batch / that product's own daily demand, as if produced alone.

Candidate PV is a sensitivity setting for the optimizer only. A product's class may then change between production versions.
SAP settings always use the fixed source reference.
The comparison with the fastest product gives the same result under both bases.

matrix_mode.title: Compatibility mode
matrix_mode.text:
Sets how AVOID pairs in the volume table are treated.
In every mode, Y pairs are compatible and N pairs are forbidden.

Avoid allowed: AVOID pairs are allowed and reported, without trying to minimize them.
Prefer compatible: AVOID pairs are allowed, but kept to a minimum before other objectives.
Strict: AVOID pairs are rejected.
Ignore table: no preference about AVOID pairs. N pairs are still forbidden.

Volume compatibility does not override filling-line eligibility.
This mode is the default for new scenarios. A scenario can change it in the Optimizer workspace.

maximum_group_size.title: Maximum group size
maximum_group_size.text:
Maximum number of products in one subgroup for this plant profile.
This is a hard limit, not a target.
A specific rule can set a tighter cap, such as two products for groups eligible for line 6.

plant-constraints.title: Plant constraints
plant-constraints.text:
Hard rules that every run using this profile must follow.
To add, change or remove one, ask the Workspace Assistant.
It asks for missing values, checks the selected dataset and shows an approval card.

Approve: saves the constraint. Nothing is saved before you click it.
Remove: deletes the constraint after confirmation.

Alternative grouping strategies belong in separate workspace runs, not here.
A line-eligibility cap does not make the optimizer prefer that line. That needs an explicit workspace objective.

sap-settings.title: SAP settings
sap-settings.text:
Rules used when SAP settings are generated for a selected scenario of a run (cycle stock at the DC, planning calendar, recipe combination, APO lot size).

They do not change the optimization. They are read when you click Generate SAP settings, so a change here applies to the next generation without running the optimizer again. Settings already generated show a warning that the profile changed; generate again to apply it.

The Assistant can explain and propose changes to these rules; you approve them on its card.

sap_calendar_odd_profile.title: Odd-week lot-size profile
sap_calendar_odd_profile.text:
Plant customizing code given to two-weekly SEFIs planned in odd weeks, written as <profile>-<calendar> (for example ODD-W1). The planning calendar uploaded to SAP is the text after '-'.

The SEFIs are sorted by forecast and split so that each half of the weeks carries about half of the volume; the SEFI with the largest forecast always gets the odd-week profile.

No default: while it is empty the Planning calendar tab is blocked. Detect from dataset reads the codes from an earlier wheel of the plant.

sap_calendar_even_profile.title: Even-week lot-size profile
sap_calendar_even_profile.text:
Plant customizing code given to two-weekly SEFIs planned in even weeks, written as <profile>-<calendar> (for example EVEN-W2). It must differ from the odd-week profile.

No default: while it is empty the Planning calendar tab is blocked.

sap_calendar_frequency_code.title: Two-weekly frequency code
sap_calendar_frequency_code.text: Production frequency code of the SEFIs that get a planning calendar (default 02W, every two weeks). FINIs with any other frequency get a reset row.

sap_calendar_lot_size.title: Calendar lot-size procedure
sap_calendar_lot_size.text: SAP lot-size procedure written for FINIs planned with the odd/even calendar (default PK).

sap_calendar_reset_lot_size.title: Reset lot-size procedure
sap_calendar_reset_lot_size.text: SAP lot-size procedure written for FINIs that leave the planning calendar (default EX).

sap_calendar_reset_text.title: Reset text
sap_calendar_reset_text.text: Text written in the calendar and profile columns of FINIs that leave the planning calendar (default: Reset via ticket - to be blank).

sap_recipe_characters.title: Fallback recipe characters
sap_recipe_characters.text:
Characters a recipe combination may use, typed in one line (for example 0123456789ABC). Each subgroup of a SEFI gets one character: digits first, then letters, then symbols.

Only used when the dataset has no RecipeCharacters table ('List of characters allowed in BW' in the inputs workbook). Empty by default; with neither, the Recipe combination and APO lot size tabs are blocked.

sap_apo_default_pv.title: APO default production version
sap_apo_default_pv.text: Production version APO already uses for every SEFI (default PV - 1). APO lot-size rows for this version are not uploaded.

sap_kpi_line_breakdown.title: Changeover KPI per filling line
sap_kpi_line_breakdown.text: Adds one changeover KPI row per filling line to the RoC and change overs tab, splitting each subgroup equally over its common lines. Off by default (site total and subgroups only).

sap_multi_tier_dc.title: Intermediate DC
sap_multi_tier_dc.text: Tick when the plant ships through an intermediate (central) DC before the selling DCs. The Central DC lot size tab then applies; it is reported as blocked because it needs sales-scenario and producing-plant ABC extractions that are not available yet. Off by default (the tab is not applicable).

sap-dc-rules.title: DC lot sizes by ABC class
sap-dc-rules.text: Cycle stock tab: for every material with forecast at a primary DC, the minimum lot size and rounding value at the DC, in pieces, depend on the material's ABC class at that DC. The All classes row applies to every class; a class row overrides it, or keeps 'Same as all classes'.

fields.Minimum lot at DC: One pallet (default), half a pallet in whole layers, one piece, a number of litres converted to pieces, or no minimum (the row then goes to the table without pallet conversion).
fields.Rounding value: Layer at maximum days, else pallet (default): one layer when the cycle days reach the maximum cycle stock, otherwise one pallet. Or always one pallet, one layer, half a pallet or one piece.
fields.Cycle days outside the wheel: Days of cycle stock for materials that are not in the wheel, by ABC class (defaults A 5, B 10, C 20). The All classes cell is for materials without an ABC class; empty skips them.
